outcome: The integer Skolem problem is still open in every source read, including a 2026 survey by the leading group; since 26 January 2024 it has moved only in restricted settings: order-4 decidability extended to all algebraic-coefficient LRS (Bacik, TheoretiCS, Dec 2025), p-adic, positive-characteristic, bounded and complexity variants, and sparsity and conditional results on 'large zeros' (Luca, Ouaknine, Worrell, MFCS 2025 and a July 2026 preprint whose decidability step is conditional on a strengthened Cramér-type conjecture), plus a September 2026 paper showing a prime-power form of the Skolem (exponential local-global) conjecture false.
problem_asks: (1) An algorithm that, given a constant-recursive (linear recurrence) sequence u, decides whether some term u_n is zero. (2) The answer must be correct for every such sequence, with no bound on the order, so the bullet asks for full decidability, not decidability for particular orders, classes, or complexity. The statement names no coefficient ring; the Wikipedia lead as read (via a summarising fetch) frames the problem over integers, rationals and algebraic numbers, so the default reading is integer coefficients with the rational and algebraic cases included. Not asked by the bullet: counting zeros, complexity, p-adic or other-ring zeros, computing the zeros, or the Skolem-Mahler-Lech finiteness theorem (classical, not in question).

events.what_happened: Mignotte, Shorey and Tijdeman, ‘The distance between terms of an algebraic recurrence sequence’, J. reine angew. Math. 349 (1984) 63–76: decidability of the zero problem for low-order recurrences, one of the 1980s breakthroughs. The original was not opened; its content is known from Bacik (arXiv 2409.01221, abstract) and Bilu (arXiv 2501.16290), and the split of order cases between this paper and Vereshchagin's is from secondary sources only.
events.delivers: Per secondary sources: decision procedure for the zero problem for algebraic linear recurrences of order 3 (with Vereshchagin, real algebraic of order 4). Uses Baker-type bounds on linear forms in logarithms.
events.remains: Algebraic order-4 recurrences with non-real roots (closed by Bacik 2024); all orders 5 and above; the general problem.

checked_by.qualification: Diophantine approximation specialist, author of the expository note
checked_by.what_they_did: Wrote an expository account of the Mignotte–Shorey–Tijdeman–Vereshchagin proofs, presenting their structure (not a verification statement)

events.direction: Positive for the orders it covers: decides the problem there.

events.what_happened: Vereshchagin, ‘Zeros of linear recursive sequences’, Dokl. Akad. Nauk SSSR 278:5 (1984) 1036–1039, and ‘Occurrence of zero in a linear recursive sequence’, Mat. Zametki 38:2 (1985) 177–189 (English: Math. Notes 38 (1985) 609–615). Independent decidability proof for order 3 and 4. Not opened; the titles differ across sources and the scope is from secondary sources (Bacik 2024 abstract; Bilu 2025; Ouaknine–Worrell ISSAC 2020 as quoted in a search summary).
events.revisions: Expanded journal version 1985 (Mat. Zametki), English translation 1985.
events.delivers: Per secondary sources: decision procedure for the zero problem of order 3 and 4 linear recurrences (scope within algebraic/real classes not confirmed from the original).
events.remains: Same as the 1984 entry: algebraic order-4 coverage (closed later by Bacik), all orders 5 and above, the general problem.

checked_by.what_they_did: Expository account of the Vereshchagin proof strategy, alongside Mignotte–Shorey–Tijdeman (no verification statement)

events.doubts: Scope and titles are from secondary sources only; the original was not read.
events.direction: Positive for the orders it covers.

events.what_happened: Lipton, Luca, Nieuwveld, Ouaknine, Purser and Worrell, ‘On the Skolem Problem and the Skolem Conjecture’, LICS 2022 (9 pp). Shows that the Skolem problem for LRS of order 5 is decidable assuming the Skolem Conjecture (the exponential local-global principle), with a concrete procedure, and that it is decidable unconditionally for reversible LRS of order 7 or less. The full text was not read; the abstract page was read.
events.delivers: Conditional on the Skolem Conjecture: decision procedure for all integer LRS of order 5. Unconditional: the problem for reversible LRS of order at most 7 (sequences that extend to a bi-infinite integer sequence). The abstract also states that for order 5 and above the problem is open.
events.remains: Unconditional decidability for integer LRS of order 5 and above; the general problem; the conditional result depends on the Skolem Conjecture.

checked_by.qualification: conference peer review of a theoretical computer science venue
checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted for LICS 2022 proceedings; no later public verification found

events.direction: Conditional positive for order 5 (under the Skolem Conjecture); unconditional positive for a reversible subclass of order at most 7.

events.what_happened: Kenison, ‘On the Skolem Problem for Reversible Sequences’, arXiv:2203.07061 (v1 14 Mar 2022; v2 11 Jul 2022; accepted at MFCS 2022 per the arXiv comment). Gives an alternative proof of the decidability for reversible LRS of order 7 or less, credited to Lipton et al.
events.delivers: Same restricted result as the LICS 2022 paper (reversible LRS of order at most 7): an alternative proof, not a new scope.
events.remains: Same as the LICS 2022 entry.
events.direction: Positive, restricted class (reversible, order at most 7).

events.what_happened: Bilu, Luca, Nieuwveld, Ouaknine, Purser and Worrell, ‘Skolem meets Schanuel’, arXiv:2204.13417 (28 Apr 2022); MFCS 2022 (LIPIcs 241, 20:1–20:15). Gives an algorithm for the Skolem problem on simple LRS (no repeated characteristic roots) whose termination is guaranteed under the Skolem Conjecture and the p-adic Schanuel Conjecture; when it halts, it outputs a certificate that the answer is correct; preliminary experiments with the Skolem tool. Abstract read; full text not read.
events.delivers: Decision procedure for simple LRS of any order, conditional on two conjectures for termination; correct output whenever it halts.
events.remains: Non-simple LRS (repeated characteristic roots); unconditional termination; the general problem.
events.doubts: Termination is conditional on the Skolem Conjecture and the p-adic Schanuel Conjecture. That is the scope of the result rather than a defect; no error report was found.
events.direction: Conditional positive, restricted class (simple LRS).

events.what_happened: Min Sha, ‘Effective results on the Skolem problem for linear recurrence sequences’, arXiv:1505.07147 (v1 26 May 2015; v6 2 Oct 2018). Explicit lower bounds on the index beyond which every term of a simple LRS of algebraic numbers is nonzero, for sequences with a dominant characteristic root or exactly two roots of maximal modulus; the abstract states that this covers almost all such sequences with rational coefficients. The exceptional set behind 'almost all' is not described on the abstract page; full text not read.
events.delivers: Within the class of simple LRS with a dominant root or exactly two roots of maximal modulus, an explicit bound reduces zero-testing to a finite check, so the problem is decidable there. Stated to cover almost all rational-coefficient sequences of that kind.
events.remains: LRS outside that class (several roots of maximal modulus beyond two, non-simple roots), and the general problem.
events.doubts: No journal reference on the arXiv page; no independent engagement found in the searches. The 'almost all' qualifier is not defined on the page read.
events.direction: Positive for a restricted class.

events.what_happened: Kenison, Lipton, Ouaknine, Worrell, ‘On the Skolem Problem and Prime Powers’, arXiv:2006.07432 (12 Jun 2020; ISSAC 2020). Studies a narrower variant: given c, is there an index of the form l·p^k (p prime, k and l at most c) at which the sequence is zero. Abstract page read only; the result's details were not read.
events.delivers: A variant: zeros restricted to prime-power-type indices with bounded parameters. Does not decide the Skolem problem as stated; the abstract describes only the variant.
events.remains: The Skolem problem itself.
events.direction: Not applicable: a restricted variant.

events.what_happened: Luca, Maynard, Noubissie, Ouaknine and Worrell, ‘Skolem Meets Bateman-Horn’, arXiv:2308.01152 (v1 2 Aug 2023; v2 20 Feb 2024; v3 5 Aug 2026). Constructs a Universal Skolem Set: a set S of positive integers for which it is decidable whether a given LRS has a zero with index in S. The arXiv v3 abstract and introduction state lower density at least 1/8 unconditionally, and density one under Martin's uniform formulation of the Bateman–Horn conjecture.
events.revisions: v2 20 Feb 2024 (inside the window; the first argument is the v1 date); v3 5 Aug 2026.
events.delivers: Restricted index set: decidability of 'has a zero with index in S' for a set S of lower density at least 1/8, unconditionally. Density one only under the Bateman–Horn hypothesis. A zero outside S is not addressed, so this is not the full problem.
events.remains: Zeros with indices outside S; the full problem (which would follow if all of N were such a set). The conditional density-one claim is superseded by the unconditional density-one result in the 2025 large-zeros paper.
events.doubts: A discrepancy in the stated lower density: the arXiv v3 abstract and introduction say 1/8, while a search summary of an MPI-hosted PDF (not opened) gives 0.29; the MPI copy may be an earlier version. No journal reference on the arXiv page.
events.direction: Positive for a restricted index set, not the full question.
events.object: A set S of positive integers, of lower density at least 1/8, such that zero-existence for LRS is decidable when restricted to indices in S (existence not explicit from the abstract read).

events.what_happened: Bilu, Luca, Nieuwveld, Ouaknine and Worrell, ‘Twisted rational zeros of linear recurrence sequences’, arXiv:2401.06537 (12 Jan 2024; one version). Introduces twisted rational zeros of non-degenerate LRS and proves each such sequence has only finitely many; computes them for the Tribonacci sequence (1/3 and −5/3 are the only non-integral ones). Published in J. London Math. Soc. 111(3) (2025) per the authors' page. Predates the window by two weeks.
events.revisions: One arXiv version; journal version JLMS 111(3), 2025.
events.delivers: Finiteness of twisted rational zeros for every non-degenerate LRS (not the integer zeros the Skolem problem asks about); effective in some cases. This is a neighbouring notion, not a decision procedure.
events.remains: The Skolem problem entirely.

checked_by.who: Journal of the London Mathematical Society (referees)

events.direction: Not applicable to decidability; a finiteness result on a neighbouring set of zeros.

events.what_happened: Jindal and Ouaknine, ‘On the Counting Complexity of the Skolem Problem’, arXiv:2403.00098 (v1 29 Feb 2024): claims that counting the zeros of an LRS is #P-hard, via a reduction from #Subset Sum and a roots-of-unity restricted variant. Version 2 (2 Aug 2025) is withdrawn by Gorav Jindal; the comment field reads 'The results in this paper are already known'. The prior source is not named and the reason for withdrawal is not given.
events.delivers: Counting complexity: #P-hardness of counting zeros. A different question from deciding whether a zero exists. Settles nothing about decidability. Its own status is withdrawn with the comment that the results were already known.
events.remains: Everything the bullet asks.
events.doubts: Withdrawn by its author; the comment says the results were already known, and the prior source is not identified, so priority is unresolved.

withdrawn.what: v2 withdrawn by Gorav Jindal; comment says 'The results in this paper are already known'; no reason given

events.direction: Does not bear on the decision question; a counting-complexity claim, now withdrawn.

events.what_happened: Bacik, ‘Completing the picture for the Skolem Problem on order-4 linear recurrence sequences’, arXiv:2409.01221 (v1 2 Sep 2024; v2 14 Jan 2025; v3 11 Jul 2025; v4 6 Oct 2025; v5 1 Dec 2025); TheoretiCS vol. 4 (2 Dec 2025), theoretics:14219, DOI 10.46298/theoretics.25.28. States: 'we show that the Skolem Problem is decidable for all algebraic LRS of order at most 4'. The 1980s work covered algebraic LRS of order at most 3 and real algebraic LRS of order at most 4. Full text read; no AI mention.
events.revisions: v2 14 Jan 2025; v3 11 Jul 2025; v4 6 Oct 2025; v5 1 Dec 2025 (TheoretiCS version, 2 Dec 2025 publication).
events.delivers: Decidability of the zero problem for all LRS of order at most 4 with algebraic coefficients. Integer and rational order-4 sequences are a subcase, already decided in 1984–85; the new content is algebraic coefficients (the 1980s results covered algebraic order at most 3 and real algebraic order at most 4). The paper's own abstract records this scope.
events.remains: All LRS of order 5 and above (over integers and over algebraic numbers); the general problem.

checked_by.qualification: expert in Diophantine approximation and the order-4 literature
checked_by.what_they_did: Expository note that presents Bacik's Theorem 1.6 and a lemma with its proof; states the note is purely expository and does not claim to verify Bacik's argument

events.direction: Positive: decides the problem for a larger coefficient class at order at most 4, which includes the integer order-4 case already known.

events.what_happened: Bilu, ‘Skolem Problem for Linear Recurrence Sequences with 4 Dominant Roots (after Mignotte, Shorey, Tijdeman, Vereshchagin and Bacik)’, arXiv:2501.16290 (v1 27 Jan 2025; v2 11 Mar 2025). Expository account of the order-4 proofs, including Bacik's contribution (Theorem 1.6 as stated in the introduction: 'The Strong Skolem Problem is decidable for a non-degenerate LRS with at most 4 distinct roots'). States 'Our contribution is purely expository, if any'. Full text read; no AI mention.
events.delivers: No new result. Exposition of the order-4 decidability, with Bacik's extension presented as Theorem 1.6.
events.remains: Everything beyond order 4.
events.doubts: The note itself does not claim verification of Bacik's argument; it presents a lemma and its proof as 'a beautiful lemma'.
events.direction: Positive for order 4 only (exposition).

events.what_happened: Bacik, Ouaknine, Purser and Worrell, ‘On the p-adic Skolem Problem’, arXiv:2504.14413 (v1 19 Apr 2025; v2 26 Sep 2025; v3 23 Jan 2026; v4 11 May 2026, which 'Contains correction to Lemma 10 of the conference proceedings version'); STACS 2026 (LIPIcs.STACS.2026.8). Algorithms that decide whether an LRS has a p-adic zero and compute the p-adic zeros, with an implementation; outputs unconditionally correct; termination subject to the p-adic Schanuel Conjecture; decidability of the Simultaneous Skolem Problem (common natural-number zero of two coprime LRS) under p-adic Schanuel. Full text read; no AI mention.
events.revisions: v2 26 Sep 2025; v3 23 Jan 2026; v4 11 May 2026 (correction to Lemma 10 of the STACS version).
events.delivers: Decision procedure (conditional termination) for p-adic zeros of LRS, and computation of p-adic zeros. The paper states that these algorithms do not solve the Skolem problem over the integers; it claims natural-number and rational zeros only under additional hypotheses, and decidability of the Simultaneous Skolem Problem under p-adic Schanuel.
events.remains: Integer and rational zeros in general, i.e. the Skolem problem as stated.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted to STACS 2026; the authors posted a full version with a correction to Lemma 10

events.doubts: Termination is conditional on the p-adic Schanuel Conjecture. The v4 correction to Lemma 10 of the proceedings version is an authors' correction, not a retraction; the implementation is reported in the paper and was not independently checked.
events.direction: Conditional positive for p-adic and simultaneous variants; explicitly not a decision of the integer problem.

events.what_happened: Bacik, Ouaknine and Worrell, ‘On the Complexity of the Skolem Problem at Low Orders’, arXiv:2507.11234 (v1 15 Jul 2025; v2 24 Oct 2025; v3 17 Jul 2026, which per the arXiv abstract page 'contains a correction to Lemma 3.2' and typo fixes). Randomised polynomial-time algorithm for the Bounded Skolem Problem (is there a zero among the first N+1 terms, N given in binary) at each fixed order; corollary: the unrestricted Skolem problem for order at most 4 lies in coRP, improving NP^RP. Peer-reviewed in the SODA 2026 proceedings per the Oxford repository record (search result, not opened). Full text of v2 read; no AI mention.
events.revisions: v2 24 Oct 2025; v3 17 Jul 2026 (correction to Lemma 3.2).
events.delivers: Complexity: the bounded problem is in randomised polynomial time for each fixed order; for the unrestricted problem this only places order at most 4 in coRP. No new order is decided.
events.remains: Decidability for order 5 and above, and the general problem; the authors state decidability is open in general.

checked_by.who: SODA 2026 programme committee (per the Oxford repository record)
checked_by.what_they_did: Peer-reviewed proceedings version (secondary record; the SIAM page was not opened)

events.doubts: v3 (17 Jul 2026) corrects Lemma 3.2 of the complexity argument. v2 read has no correction note; v3 full text was not read, so the size and effect of the correction are unknown.
events.direction: Complexity improvement at order at most 4; no new decidability.

events.what_happened: Le and Miyazaki, ‘Purely exponential Diophantine equations with four terms of consecutive bases: contribution to Skolem's conjecture’, arXiv:2508.17601 (25 Aug 2025). For n^x = (n+1)^y + (n+2)^z + (n+3)^w, the only positive-integer solutions are (n,x,y,z,w) = (2,5,1,1,2) and (3,3,2,1,1); for each n ≥ 4 an explicit modulus with no solutions. Framed as a contribution to Skolem's local-global problem for exponential Diophantine equations. Abstract page read; the word 'linear recurrence' does not appear.
events.delivers: A different problem that shares a namesake (Skolem's conjecture on exponential Diophantine equations, not the zero problem for LRS). Classifies solutions of one family of exponential equations.
events.remains: The Skolem problem for LRS entirely.
events.direction: Not applicable: different problem.

events.what_happened: Dong and Shafrir, ‘The Skolem Problem in rings of positive characteristic’, arXiv:2510.27603 (v1 31 Oct 2025; v2 5 Nov 2025, 'Corrected a small error in Lemma 3.2'; v3 11 Mar 2026). The Skolem problem is decidable in finitely generated commutative rings of positive characteristic; the algorithm takes a finite presentation of the ring and the LRS. Proof uses Dong–Shafrir's S-unit result (arXiv 2505.19141) and Karimov–Luca–Nieuwveld–Ouaknine–Worrell (2025). Full text read; no AI mention.
events.revisions: v2 5 Nov 2025 (correction to Lemma 3.2); v3 11 Mar 2026 (citation updated to 2026).
events.delivers: Decidability for LRS over finitely generated commutative rings of characteristic T > 0. The paper states: 'the decidability of the Skolem Problem over the ring ℤ remains open'. Characteristic-zero rings, including the integers, are not addressed.
events.remains: Integers and all characteristic-zero rings (the default integer reading of the bullet).
events.direction: Positive, different ring setting; the paper says the integer case is open.

events.what_happened: Bacik and Varonka, ‘On the Subspace Orbit Problem and the Simultaneous Skolem Problem’, arXiv:2601.18349 (v1 26 Jan 2026; v2 14 May 2026); LICS 2026 (LIPIcs 380, 8:1–8:27; publication date 9 Jul 2026 per the Dagstuhl record). The Orbit problem is decidable for targets of logarithmic dimension in the orbit dimension; when the target dimension is linear, the problem is as hard as the Skolem problem; the codimension-1 case is equivalent to the Skolem problem for LRS. The abstract states no result on the Simultaneous Skolem Problem. Abstract page and most of the full text read; the end of the HTML was truncated and unread.
events.delivers: Decidability for a different problem (the Orbit problem) in a restricted dimension regime. The hardness statement is a reduction from Skolem to a subspace orbit problem, not a decision of Skolem. The codimension-1 equivalence restates Skolem in orbit language.
events.remains: The Skolem problem itself.

checked_by.what_they_did: Accepted and published in LICS 2026 proceedings

events.direction: Neighbouring problem; the Skolem equivalence and hardness statements are reductions, not solutions.

events.what_happened: Luca, Ouaknine and Worrell, ‘On Large Zeros of Linear Recurrence Sequences’, MFCS 2025 (LIPIcs 345, 71:1–71:11; DOI 10.4230/LIPIcs.MFCS.2025.71; publication date 20 Aug 2025; no earlier arXiv preprint found, so this is a proceedings date and may not be the first public argument). A 'large' zero of a non-degenerate LRS is one whose index n is at least 2·exp⁶(C_u), a sixth-fold exponential of the data's size. Proves that the set of integers that can be large zeros has null density, which yields a Universal Skolem Set of density one unconditionally; defines a density-one set of 'good' primes; conjectures that large zeros do not exist, which would entail decidability. Full text read through the HTML version; no AI mention.
events.revisions: The 2026 arXiv version (next entry) changes the threshold to a double exponential and states the conclusion as conditional on a Cramér-type conjecture rather than as a conjecture.
events.delivers: Unconditional: the index set of possible large zeros has null density, giving a density-one Universal Skolem Set (restricted index set). It does not decide any LRS: the decision step, that large zeros do not exist, is only conjectured here.
events.remains: Whether large zeros exist (the conjecture); zeros below the threshold are not addressed by this result; the Skolem problem as stated.
events.doubts: The 2026 version gives a different threshold and different status for the conclusion, so the two versions do not state the same claim. Only the 2026 version's Theorem 4.3 and Conjecture 4.2 were read in full; the MFCS HTML version was read for its definitions.
events.direction: Partial: an unconditional sparsity result that supports decidability only via an unproven conjecture.

events.what_happened: Luca, Ouaknine and Worrell, ‘Conjectural Decidability of the Skolem Problem’, arXiv:2607.15510 (v1 16 Jul 2026; single version; 20 pages per the authors' page). Large zeros are defined with a double exponential threshold, n ≥ exp(exp(10H log H)) in the height H of the sequence. Unconditionally: the set of positive integers that can be large zeros of some LRS has null density, so a density-one Universal Skolem Set exists. Conditionally on Conjecture 4.2, a Cramér–Granville-type strengthening for consecutive 'good' primes, large zeros of sufficiently high LRS do not exist (Theorem 4.3 as read), which the authors say would entail decidability. Full text read; no AI mention.
events.delivers: (a) Unconditional: null density of possible large-zero indices, hence a density-one Universal Skolem Set. (b) Conditional on Conjecture 4.2: no large zeros for sufficiently high-height LRS, which the authors say yields decidability. The text read does not spell out how the 'sufficiently high' case is completed, so full decidability is conditional and the final step was not confirmed.
events.remains: Unconditional decidability for all LRS; the conditioning conjecture; the finite low-height cases as the text was read.
events.doubts: The decidability conclusion depends on Conjecture 4.2, a strengthened Cramér-type hypothesis that is not proven. The threshold differs from the 2025 version (sixth-fold versus double exponential), so claims about 'large zeros' are not comparable across versions without checking.
events.direction: Conditional positive: the authors claim a decision procedure under an unproven number-theoretic conjecture; unconditional result is a sparsity statement.

events.what_happened: Dong and Shafrir, ‘Skolem-Mahler-Lech in rings of positive characteristic: a shorter proof and a multi-dimensional generalization’, arXiv:2609.03127 (v1 2 Sep 2026; single version). A shorter proof of their 2026 result, via the Derksen–Masser S-unit theorem as a black box; a multi-dimensional Skolem–Mahler–Lech generalisation for finite-characteristic modules (zero sets are finite intersections of effectively computable p-normal sets); a decision procedure for whether two classical LRS share a value over characteristic p^a or p^a q^b. Full text read; no AI mention.
events.delivers: Positive characteristic only (ℓM = 0): a shorter proof and a multi-dimensional generalisation, plus a common-value decision procedure. The integers are not addressed.
events.remains: Integers and characteristic-zero rings.
events.direction: Positive, positive-characteristic setting only.

events.what_happened: Bacik, ‘Twisted Rational Zeros and Local-Global Principles for Linear Recurrence Sequences’, arXiv:2609.16392 (v1 14 Sep 2026; single version; 23 pages). Claims, per the abstract and introduction as read: (i) unconditional characterisation of when twisted rational zeros are p-adic zeros for infinitely many primes, answering two questions of Bilu et al. (2025); (ii) a counterexample to the prime-power strengthening of the Skolem Conjecture (the exponential local-global principle), explained through twisted rational zeros; (iii) conditional on the p-adic Schanuel Conjecture, a local-global principle for simultaneous zeros of two coprime LRS; (iv) a heuristic conjecture that twisted rational zeros are the only obstruction to the strengthened form. The paper says it 'is related to, but does not resolve, the decidability of the Skolem Problem'. Its AI declaration (end of Section 5) reads, per the HTML fetch: 'ChatGPT 5.6 Sol was used for literature search, and for reviewing the paper for mathematical and writing errors/typos.' / 'A non-trivial error was found by ChatGPT in an early version of the proof of Theorem 28, which was subsequently corrected by the author.' / 'A mild simplification of the last part of the proof of Theorem 22 was also suggested by ChatGPT and incorporated into the final draft.' / 'Everything else, and all text in the article is human-generated.' See summary on why this is not recorded under ai.systems.
events.delivers: (i)–(iii) concern local-global and p-adic behaviour of LRS and simultaneous zeros; (ii) shows a prime-power form of the Skolem Conjecture false (per the abstract as read); none of these decides whether an integer LRS has a zero. The Skolem problem is stated as open.
events.remains: Decidability of the Skolem problem over the integers; conjecture (iv) (heuristic only).
events.doubts: Single author; no public proof-level check found. The only check on record is the author's own AI-assisted review, described in the AI declaration. Conjecture (iv) is explicitly heuristic. The record does not establish whether any earlier conditional result depends on the prime-power form that (ii) refutes.
events.direction: Cuts against a strengthened, prime-power form of the Skolem Conjecture; does not bear on decidability over the integers directly.

events.what_happened: Bacik, Karimov, Luca, Nieuwveld, Ouaknine, Purser and Worrell, ‘A survey of the Skolem and Positivity Problems for linear recurrence sequences’ (submitted, 2026; 59 pages; listed on Ouaknine's MPI-SWS page with no arXiv identifier or venue). Abstract page read; the PDF was not readable as text. Surveys the state of the art; states that the decidability of both problems has been open for many decades; exhibits two concrete integer LRS, of orders 6 and 10, for which the authors cannot solve the Skolem and Positivity Problems respectively. A search summary gives the date as 26 July 2026; this is unverified.
events.delivers: No new decidability claimed in the abstract read; a status statement: integer Skolem open in general, with order at most 4 decided and order 5 and above not.
events.remains: Everything the bullet asks.
events.doubts: The authors are the leading group in this area; the survey is not an independent check. Full PDF text was not read.
events.direction: Status statement: problem open.

disputes.summary: Jindal and Ouaknine's counting-complexity preprint (arXiv 2403.00098) was withdrawn in August 2025 with the comment 'The results in this paper are already known'. The prior source the comment refers to is not named in the record.

A search summary of the 2026 survey says an earlier announced proof of decidability for order 5 was flagged, in a later paper, as having a serious gap. I could not identify the announcement, its authors, or the gap, and the survey's text was not readable to confirm the claim. Treat as unverified. The 2022 LICS abstract does not mention any such claim.

summary: Forty-one searches and about forty-five fetches (abstract pages, HTML full texts and PDFs; most PDFs were unreadable as binary) were run. The integer Skolem problem is not settled in any source read, and the most recent survey (2026, by the leading group) lists it as open for many decades, with concrete open examples of orders 6 and 10. Since 26 January 2024, movement is confined to restricted settings. (1) Bacik (arXiv September 2024; TheoretiCS December 2025) decides the problem for all LRS of order at most 4 with algebraic coefficients. The integer order-4 case was already known from 1984–85 (Mignotte–Shorey–Tijdeman; Vereshchagin), so the new content is the algebraic coefficient class. (2) Bacik–Ouaknine–Purser–Worrell (April 2025) give p-adic zero algorithms, conditional on the p-adic Schanuel Conjecture, and state that they do not solve the integer problem; Bacik–Ouaknine–Worrell (July 2025) give a randomised polynomial-time bounded problem, placing order-4 Skolem in coRP. (3) Dong and Shafrir (October 2025; shorter proof and generalisation September 2026) decide the problem in finitely generated commutative rings of positive characteristic and state the integer case is open. (4) Luca, Ouaknine and Worrell: MFCS 2025 proves that the set of possible large-zero indices has null density, giving an unconditional density-one Universal Skolem Set, and conjectures that large zeros do not exist, which would decide the problem; a July 2026 arXiv version gives the same unconditional sparsity result and makes the decision step conditional on a strengthened Cramér-type conjecture (Conjecture 4.2). (5) Bacik (14 September 2026) shows a prime-power form of the Skolem (exponential local-global) conjecture false and proves conditional local-global results; this does not decide the integer problem. Discounted or neighbouring events, recorded in full: Jindal–Ouaknine counting complexity (withdrawn; the comment says the results were already known); Bacik–Varonka orbit problem (Skolem reductions only); Le–Miyazaki (a different Skolem conjecture, on exponential Diophantine equations); the 2023 Universal Skolem Set (lower density 1/8, density one only conditionally, now superseded by the unconditional density-one result). Older events are recorded because the status depends on them: the 1984–85 order-3/4 results; LICS 2022 (order 5 under the Skolem Conjecture; reversible LRS of order at most 7); MFCS 2022 simple-LRS algorithm (conditional on two conjectures); Sha 2015–2018 (a restricted class with explicit bounds). Close calls. (a) Whether the algebraic order-4 result counts as resolving 'the problem' turns on whether the bullet's 'constant-recursive sequence' includes algebraic coefficients: the Wikipedia lead, as read through a summarising fetch, frames the problem over integers, rationals and algebraic numbers, and the bullet names none. (b) The 2026 decision route is conditional on an unproven Cramér-type hypothesis, and the record does not confirm how the 'sufficiently high' case is completed. (c) The 2025 and 2026 versions define 'large zeros' differently: the MFCS HTML gives n ≥ 2·exp⁶(C_u); the 2026 full text gives n ≥ exp(exp(10H log H)). They are not the same set. AI involvement. A targeted AI search (AlphaEvolve, AlphaProof, Deep Think, GPT-5, o3, Erdős-problems and AI-tracker listings, LLM counterexample searches, Lean/Mathlib formalisations) found nothing connecting any AI system to the Skolem problem. The only AI disclosure in the record is in arXiv 2609.16392. Its AI declaration, read from the HTML full text, says 'ChatGPT 5.6 Sol' was used for literature search and for checking for mathematical and writing errors; that ChatGPT found a non-trivial error in an early version of a proof (corrected by the author); and that it suggested a mild simplification of the last part of another proof, which was incorporated; 'Everything else, and all text in the article is human-generated.' Under §5.4 I did not place this under ai.systems: the uses are checking, literature search, and a suggestion to simplify a proof whose result was already established, so the involvement is not load-bearing on the result. Hence ai.none_found is false for that event with systems empty. The theorem numbers in the declaration are not settled: the direct fetch gives Theorem 28 and Theorem 22, while a search summary gives Theorem 29 and Theorem 23, and the quotes above come from the direct fetch. Every other event's full text (or, where unreadable, its abstract page) carries no AI mention. Where only an abstract page was read (Min Sha 2015–2018; LICS 2022; MFCS 2022 simple-LRS paper; Le–Miyazaki; Kenison-Lipton-Ouaknine-Worrell 2020; the 2026 survey; the Bacik–Varonka paper's HTML was read to about 100,000 characters only), none_found reflects the abstract read, not a full-text check. The 1984–85 originals were not opened at all; their none_found reflects their date only and is labelled as such in the event. No Wikipedia-era statement of the problem needs changing from the sources read, though the Wikipedia article (read through a summarising fetch, last edited 24 May 2026) cites no work after 2022.
competing_reading: The strongest case for a different reading: (a) the Bacik order-4 result (and the Luca–Ouaknine–Worrell 2026 conditional decision route) could be read as resolving the bullet in a restricted or conditional sense, since the bullet does not say 'over the integers' and the Wikipedia lead covers algebraic numbers; (b) a reader who accepts Conjecture 4.2 of arXiv 2607.15510 could count the Skolem problem as conditionally decided from July 2026; (c) the Bacik declaration's ChatGPT simplification of the last part of a proof, incorporated into the final draft, could be read as load-bearing on the paper's main theorem (I excluded it on the §5.4 test that the result would have been established without it, but a reader who sees it as a substantive mathematical suggestion would count it); (d) a reader who puts the 2025 MFCS version's 'large zeros do not exist' conjecture and the 2026 conditional theorem in one line of development would read the trajectory as steady progress, where another reads two different definitions of the set.
what_would_settle_it: (1) For the integer problem: an unconditional decision procedure for integer LRS of order 5 or above, or a proof of the conditioning conjecture (Conjecture 4.2 in arXiv 2607.15510), or an expert verdict on the completion of the 'sufficiently high' case in that paper. (2) For the algebraic reading: a judgement on whether the bullet's 'constant-recursive sequence' includes algebraic coefficients, which only the judging pass can make. (3) For the 2026 version of the large-zeros argument: a referee report, or an expert digest, on Theorem 4.3 and on whether the threshold change between the MFCS 2025 and 2026 versions alters the claim. (4) For the AI declaration: the PDF text of arXiv 2609.16392 (not readable here), to confirm the theorem numbers and the exact wording of the four quoted sentences. (5) For the order-5 'gap' claim in the disputes: the survey's full text, or the paper it cites.
incomplete: Not fully done. (a) Not opened or not readable: the PDFs of arXiv 2609.16392, the 2026 survey, the MFCS 2025 'large zeros' paper (its HTML version was read instead), and the LICS 2026 paper (metadata only); the 1984 Mignotte–Shorey–Tijdeman paper, the 1984/1985 Vereshchagin papers, the Lipton et al. LICS 2022 paper, the Bilu et al. 2022 paper, Min Sha's full text, the Luca–Maynard–Noubissie–Ouaknine–Worrell 2023 preprint's MPI PDF (0.29 bound), and the 2022 'positive lower density' Universal Skolem Set preprint were not read in full or at all. (b) Partly read: arXiv 2601.18349 v2 (read to about 100,000 characters of a longer text; the remainder was unavailable); arXiv 2507.11234 (v2 read in full; v3, which corrects Lemma 3.2, was not read); arXiv 2308.01152 v3 (read to about 100,000 of 123,806 characters); arXiv 2401.06537 (read to the point where the text was truncated, which is after the main results). (c) Search only, not opened: the TheoretiCS page for 2409.01221 (the journal details come from the arXiv page); the Oxford repository record for the SODA 2026 venue; Tao's 2007 blog post (background only); the Quanta and erdosproblems.com searches (no hits); the Karimov–Luca–Nieuwveld–Ouaknine–Worrell 2025 paper (arXiv 2407.05191, a dependency of Dong–Shafrir), and the Ouaknine–Worrell 2014 Positivity paper (about Positivity, not Skolem, but cited for the order-6 barrier). (d) The Wikipedia article was read only through a summarising fetch, so statements about its current lead come from that fetch. (e) The date of the 2026 survey (26 July 2026) is from a search summary, and the claim of a gap in an earlier order-5 proof is unidentified. (f) The AI declaration's theorem numbers disagree between the direct fetch (28, 22) and a search summary (29, 23); this is unresolved.

event.what_happened: Bacik, ‘Completing the picture for the Skolem Problem on order-4 linear recurrence sequences’, arXiv:2409.01221 (v1 2 Sep 2024; v2 14 Jan 2025; v3 11 Jul 2025; v4 6 Oct 2025; v5 1 Dec 2025); TheoretiCS vol. 4 (2 Dec 2025), theoretics:14219, DOI 10.46298/theoretics.25.28. States: 'we show that the Skolem Problem is decidable for all algebraic LRS of order at most 4'. The 1980s work covered algebraic LRS of order at most 3 and real algebraic LRS of order at most 4. Full text read; no AI mention.
event.revisions: v2 14 Jan 2025; v3 11 Jul 2025; v4 6 Oct 2025; v5 1 Dec 2025 (TheoretiCS version, 2 Dec 2025 publication).
event.delivers: Decidability of the zero problem for all LRS of order at most 4 with algebraic coefficients. Integer and rational order-4 sequences are a subcase, already decided in 1984–85; the new content is algebraic coefficients (the 1980s results covered algebraic order at most 3 and real algebraic order at most 4). The paper's own abstract records this scope.
event.remains: All LRS of order 5 and above (over integers and over algebraic numbers); the general problem.

event.direction: Positive: decides the problem for a larger coefficient class at order at most 4, which includes the integer order-4 case already known.

judgement.why: The statement asks for a decision procedure for all constant-recursive sequences; no event gives one unconditionally. Bacik 2024 decides all algebraic-coefficient LRS of order at most 4, a restriction (by order) of the question that is new only if the statement's sequences include algebraic coefficients, as the Wikipedia framing does; scored case, digested via TheoretiCS publication. The 1984-85 and 2022 reversible/order results are pre-snapshot cases. Conditional decision procedures (Skolem Meets Schanuel, the 2026 Cramér-conditional paper) are reductions to unproven conjectures, so none. Restricted-index (Universal Skolem Set), p-adic, positive-characteristic, complexity, counting, twisted-zero and exponential-Diophantine results answer changed questions: variant. The Bacik 2026 AI declaration describes ChatGPT doing literature search, error finding (criticism) and a 'mild simplification' of an already-proved argument; that is checking/editing, not mathematics in the result, so none, consistent with the empty systems list.
judgement.doubts: Bacik 2024 as a case depends on reading the statement to include algebraic coefficients; for integer LRS order 4 was already decided in 1984-85, and on a strict integer reading the event adds nothing to the stated question. Treating LICS/MFCS acceptance as digestion is a judgment call. The unidentified order-5 'gap' claim in disputes could not be assessed.
